transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’ve been… preoccupied with something. It feels like certain people around the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are paying attention to who I meet with—clients, mostly—and sort of sending signals through invitations, panel topics, even where people sit near me at events.

I know it might sound like coincidence. I tell myself that. But I can’t really shake it.
Do you think these people are actually trying to communicate something to you, or is it just a feeling you have?

I… I think they are trying to communicate something. Not openly, but through little things—who invites me where, the topics at panels, who ends up sitting near me. I know it could be coincidence, but it doesn’t feel that way, and I can’t really let it go.
Do you believe these signals are meant for you specifically, or could they be intended for someone else?

I think… they’re meant for me. I mean, it’s about who I’m meeting with, my clients, the events I go to. Maybe someone else could miss it, but it feels directed at me specifically. Even when I try to tell myself it’s nothing, I can’t really drop it.
Do you think there's a specific message or goal behind what you believe these people are trying to communicate to you?

I think the goal is… to let me know they’re aware of who I’m meeting with. Like clients, mostly. Maybe to influence who I work with, or just make it clear they’re watching. It’s not one clear message, exactly, but the pattern feels directed at me. Even when I try to write it off, I can’t really.
Do you think there's anything that could convince you that these signals aren't actually being sent?

I don’t know. Maybe if there was some clear explanation for all of it, like proof the invitations or seating were random. But even when I tell myself it’s probably coincidence, it still feels too connected to who I’m meeting with. It’s hard for me to just drop it.
How long have you been feeling like you're receiving these signals?
About… two months, I think. That’s when I started noticing it with the client meetings and the signals.
Have you ever had a moment where you doubted these signals were real?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve had moments where I tell myself it’s probably just coincidence. Like the invitations, the panel topics, where people sit at events… maybe it could all be normal.

But then it lines up with clients I’m meeting, and I can’t really let it go. It still feels like certain people are tracking it somehow.
Do you think there's any way to stop or change the signals you believe are being sent to you?

I’m not really sure. I guess if I stopped going to those events or kept my client meetings more private, maybe it would quiet down. But… it feels like the signals are already sort of built into the invitations and topics and who’s around me, so I don’t know how I’d actually stop it.
Do you think it's possible for you to be completely wrong about these signals being sent to you?

I guess… technically, yeah, it’s possible I’m wrong. I try to tell myself it could just be coincidence.

But it doesn’t feel that way most of the time. When the invitations or panel topics line up with clients I’ve met, or certain people end up sitting near me, it’s hard for me to just dismiss it completely.
Do you think there's anything that could happen that would completely change your mind about these signals being sent to you?

I don’t know. Maybe if there was some clear proof that nobody in those circles knew anything about my client meetings, or that the invitations and topics were decided completely separately… maybe that would help.

But honestly, even then, I think I’d still wonder. It’s hard for me to fully let it go when it keeps seeming to line up.
Do you believe the signals you're receiving are from a normal, everyday kind of person or group, or is it something more unusual?

I think it’s… regular people, mostly. Like people in the arts and finance circles around Cincinnati. Not something supernatural or anything.

It just feels like they know who I’ve been meeting with, and then little things show up at events… invitations, panel topics, who ends up near me. I know that sounds like maybe coincidence, but it doesn’t feel that way to me.
Have your beliefs about these signals changed in intensity or certainty over the two months you've been noticing them?

Yeah… I think it’s gotten stronger over the two months.

At first I could kind of brush it off as coincidence, but the more the invitations and topics seemed to line up with clients I’d met, the harder it got to let go of. I’m not saying I’m 100% certain, but… I feel pretty convinced most of the time.
Are these beliefs about signals affecting your ability to work with clients or interact with people in your daily life?

Yeah… a bit.

I’m still working, but I’ve missed some follow-ups, and I don’t keep in touch with clients as much as I used to. I’ve also been avoiding some public panels. So… my practice has gotten smaller. I don’t really like saying that, but it has.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about these signals being sent to you, or do you feel that your belief about them is absolute?

I don’t know if I’d call it absolute.

I can tell myself it might just be coincidence, and part of me knows that’s possible. But when the invitations or panel topics line up with who I’ve been meeting… or certain people sit near me at events, it’s hard to shake. I can’t really let it go, even when I try.
Have these beliefs about signals being sent to you caused you significant distress or anxiety?

Yeah… it has.

I try not to let it show, but it makes me anxious. When I get an invitation or hear about a panel topic, I start wondering what they know, or why that person is sitting nearby. Even if I tell myself it could be nothing, I can’t really drop it, and that’s… stressful.
Have these beliefs about signals being sent to you affected your personal relationships with friends or family?

A little, I guess… I don’t really talk about it much with friends or family.

The bigger thing is work. I’m still working, but I’ve missed follow-ups and I don’t keep up with clients like I used to. I’ve been avoiding some panels too, so… my practice is smaller now.
Are you having trouble with daily activities outside of work due to these beliefs about signals?

Mostly it’s work.

Outside of that… I don’t think it’s changed a lot. The main problem is I’m still working, but I’ve missed follow-ups, avoided some public panels, and I’m not keeping up with clients the way I used to. So my practice has gotten smaller.
Do you believe the people sending you these signals have a rational or logical reason for doing so?

I… I think they must have a reason, yes. It feels logical to me, like they’re tracking who I meet with or what circles I’m moving in.

I know some of it could look like coincidence, but when the invitations or panel topics line up, or certain people end up sitting near me… it’s hard for me to just dismiss it.
Do you think the messages you believe are being sent to you are unusual or hard for others to understand?

Yeah… I guess it probably sounds unusual to other people.

I don’t usually explain it because it’s hard to make it sound reasonable out loud. But to me, when invitations or panel topics line up with who I’ve been meeting, or certain people end up near me at events… it feels like it means something. Even when I tell myself it could be coincidence, I can’t really drop it.
